question.problem:
Solve the linear congruence $2x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,7)$ using trial and error. Express your answer as a nonnegative integer smaller than $7.$

$x≡$
{{field-1}}$\,(\text{mod}\,7)$
question.worked_solution:
Since the modulus $n=7$ is fairly small, we can solve the congruence by trial and error. 

Substituting $x=0,1,2,3,4,5,6$ into the congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot 0 & ≡0≢1 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) &  & \times  \\ 2\cdot 1 & ≡2≢1 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) &  & \times  \\ 2\cdot 2 & ≡4≢1 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) &  & \times  \\ 2\cdot 3 & ≡6≢1 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) &  & \times  \\ 2\cdot 4 & ≡8≡7+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) &  & ✓ \\ 2\cdot 5 & ≡10≡7+3≡3≢1 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) &  & \times  \\ 2\cdot 6 & ≡12≡7+5≡5≢1 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) &  & \times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡4\,(\text{mod}\,7).$

**Note**: Any number congruent to $4$ modulo $7$ is a solution. For example, note that $11≡4,$ and this also satisfies our congruence:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & ≡2\cdot 11\, &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡22\, &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡3\cdot 7+1\, &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡0+1\, &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡1\,\,✓\, &  & (\text{mod}\,7)\end{aligned}
$$
